note:
THE ARCHIVE'S OWN WORD ON WHICH SCANS IT HOLDS, WHAT RECORD EACH BELONGS TO, AND WHETHER ITS RULES LET IT SHOW THEM, plus the records it holds a public address for and the ledger entries it will not link to. tools/build-records.py reads this file with site/src/data/evidence.json and writes site/src/data/records.json, the table the <Rec> component draws every record link from (linking standard, L3 and L4). Edit by hand, with the reason, in a commit that says why.

SHOW. A scan is `show: true` only where the archive's rules say so: images from the Landesarchiv Berlin, the Berlin directories (ZLB), the Archiwum Państwowe w Bydgoszczy, the Reichsgesetzblatt, family papers in the family's keeping, and the Rosebank register page the parish supplied for this archive. NEVER shown here, whatever else is said: a Findmypast, GenDatabase, Arolsen, FamilySearch, MyHeritage or NAA image (link-only), a Matricula image (link-only until David rules), and anything that prints a living or possibly living person's name, address or an identity, tax or licence number (see `withheld`). Only a scan already published on a page of this site is listed: this file places no new scan on the site, it lets a page show a published one beside the passage that cites it.

withheld.reason: The 2010 death-certificate scan and the 2010 declaration scan are withheld (commits 7e4c71f and 1992a19): they print a possibly living physician's address and licence number, and a declarant's street address. The ledger entry stays linkable; no plate is attached to it and none may be.

hold.reason: The 1965 roll lists two children who are flagged living in the family tree. The passage that relies on it stays plain text; the ledger entry is not linked from a narrative page.
The National Archives of Australia catalogue names the same two living children (the archive's own rule is stricter than the public catalogue). Same: not linked.
